title: October records reversed one recorded ozone contrast after flower visits ended in a North Wales experiment in 2021
abstract: We tested whether exposure after the last flower visits changed a recorded warming comparison in a North Wales experiment. At the 80 ppb ozone target, heated minus ambient means were -0.830 ppb for June-September 2021 and +3.977 ppb with October added. October supplied 17.016 percent of valid hours and a +27.422 ppb contrast. The other two targets did not reverse. Equal day weights, clock-hour restriction, two October endpoints and all single seven-day block omissions kept the reversal. Two missing-hour bounds kept it under an assumed 0-200 ppb range. A reading-error bound of 0.415 ppb per reading can remove the negative pre-October sign. Thus the result concerns released records, not calibrated true doses. One dome per treatment, one site-year and month-only flower visits prevent causal plant claims and independent regional validation. Original code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and external retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: Recorded paired ozone contrasts by window and cumulative endpoint. October follows all recorded flower visits. Lines show fixed-record summaries, not confidence intervals.
